title: Ezekiel Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 11.

questions.question: Who were the two princes of the people mentioned among the twenty-five men at the east gate of the LORD's house?
options: Jaazaniah the son of Azur and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah
Micaiah the son of Imlah and Elijah the prophet
Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah and Ahab the son of Kolaiah
Ezekiel and Jeremiah
questions.correctAnswer: Jaazaniah the son of Azur and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:1 specifically names Jaazaniah the son of Azur and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah as princes among the twenty-five men at the east gate.

questions.question: What did the men at the gate devise and give in the city according to Ezekiel?
options: Mischief and wicked counsel
Peace and prosperity
Justice and mercy
Grain and wine
questions.correctAnswer: Mischief and wicked counsel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:2 states that these men devise mischief and give wicked counsel in the city.

questions.question: What metaphor do the men use to describe the city and themselves in their counsel?
options: This city is the caldron, and we be the flesh
This city is a vineyard, and we are the branches
This city is a fortress, and we are the stones
This city is a garden, and we are the flowers
questions.correctAnswer: This city is the caldron, and we be the flesh
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:3 records the men's saying that the city is the caldron and they are the flesh.

questions.question: What command is given to the son of man regarding the men that devise mischief?
options: Prophesy against them
Ignore them
Join them
Build houses with them
questions.correctAnswer: Prophesy against them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:4 instructs the son of man to prophesy against the men who devise mischief.

questions.question: What does the Spirit of the LORD say about the thoughts of the house of Israel?
options: He knows every one of the things that come into their mind
He is unaware of their thoughts
He only knows their righteous thoughts
He judges only their actions, not thoughts
questions.correctAnswer: He knows every one of the things that come into their mind
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:5 states that the LORD knows all the thoughts that come into the minds of the house of Israel.

questions.question: What have the people done in the city according to Ezekiel 11:6?
options: Multiplied the slain and filled the streets with the slain
Built many houses
Sowed fields of grain
Built altars to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Multiplied the slain and filled the streets with the slain
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:6 clearly states that the people have multiplied their slain and filled the streets with them.

questions.question: What will the LORD do with the people who have made the city a caldron with the slain as the flesh?
options: Bring them forth out of the midst of it
Destroy them all immediately
Let them remain in the city forever
Send angels to protect them
questions.correctAnswer: Bring them forth out of the midst of it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:7 says that although the city is the caldron and the slain are the flesh, the LORD will bring the people out of the midst of it.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will bring upon the people who have feared the sword?
options: A sword
Peace
A harvest of grain
A new king
questions.correctAnswer: A sword
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:8 states that because the people feared the sword, the LORD will bring a sword upon them.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 11:9, into whose hands will the LORD deliver the people?
options: Strangers
Angels
Kings of Israel
Their own people
questions.correctAnswer: Strangers
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:9 says the LORD will deliver the people into the hands of strangers and execute judgments among them.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel was brought to the west gate of the LORD's house in the vision described in Ezekiel 11:1.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:1 states he was brought to the east gate of the LORD's house, not the west gate.

questions.question: True or False: Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died when Ezekiel prophesied, causing him to cry out to the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:13 records that when Ezekiel prophesied, Pelatiah died, and Ezekiel fell on his face and cried out to the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: The glory of the LORD departed from the city and stood upon the mountain on the west side of the city.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:23 states the glory of the LORD stood upon the mountain on the east side of the city, not the west.

questions.question: True or False: The Spirit took Ezekiel in a vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea to the captives.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:24 confirms that the Spirit took Ezekiel in a vision to Chaldea to those of the captivity.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 11, which event happens first?
options: The spirit lifts Ezekiel to the east gate of the LORD's house
Pelatiah the son of Benaiah dies
The glory of the LORD goes up from the midst of the city
The LORD promises to gather Israel from the countries
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit lifts Ezekiel to the east gate of the LORD's house
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:1 describes the spirit lifting Ezekiel to the east gate first, with the other events occurring later in the chapter.

questions.question: What will God replace the stony heart with according to Ezekiel 11?
options: A heart of flesh
A heart of stone
A heart of gold
A heart of iron
questions.correctAnswer: A heart of flesh
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:19 says God will take the stony heart out and give them a heart of flesh.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 11:10, where does God say He will judge the people who fall by the sword?
options: In the border of Israel
In the city of Jerusalem
In the land of Egypt
In the temple of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: In the border of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:10 states, 'Ye shall fall by the sword; I will judge you in the border of Israel,' indicating that the judgment will take place at the border of Israel.

questions.question: What reason does Ezekiel 11:12 give for God's judgment on the people?
options: They have not walked in God's statutes and followed the manners of heathen
They have built too many houses
They have worshipped idols openly
They have neglected the poor and widows
questions.correctAnswer: They have not walked in God's statutes and followed the manners of heathen
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:12 explains that the people are judged because they 'have not walked in my statutes, neither executed my judgments, but have done after the manners of the heathen that are round about you.'

questions.question: What happened to Pelatiah the son of Benaiah when Ezekiel prophesied, according to Ezekiel 11:13?
options: He died
He repented
He was exiled
He was imprisoned
questions.correctAnswer: He died
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:13 states, 'And it came to pass, when I prophesied, that Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died,' showing the immediate consequence upon the prophecy.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 11:15 describe the attitude of the inhabitants of Jerusalem towards the house of Israel?
options: They told them to get far from the LORD and claimed the land as their possession
They welcomed them to worship the LORD together
They sought peace and unity with them
They invited them to rebuild the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They told them to get far from the LORD and claimed the land as their possession
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:15 says the inhabitants of Jerusalem told the house of Israel, 'Get you far from the LORD: unto us is this land given in possession,' indicating rejection and claiming the land for themselves.

questions.question: What does God promise to be for the scattered Israelites in the countries where they dwell, as stated in Ezekiel 11:16?
options: A little sanctuary
A mighty fortress
A great deliverer
A fearsome judge
questions.correctAnswer: A little sanctuary
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:16 declares, 'yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come,' promising God's protective presence despite their dispersion.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 11:17, what will God do for His scattered people?
options: Gather them from the peoples and give them the land of Israel
Punish them for their sins
Make them slaves in foreign lands
Hide them from their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Gather them from the peoples and give them the land of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:17 states, 'I will even gather you from the people, and assemble you out of the countries where ye have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel,' promising restoration and return.

questions.question: What will the people do when they return to the land, according to Ezekiel 11:18?
options: Take away all detestable things and abominations
Rebuild idols and altars
Oppress their neighbors
Ignore God's laws
questions.correctAnswer: Take away all detestable things and abominations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:18 promises, 'they shall take away all the detestable things thereof and all the abominations thereof from thence,' emphasizing purification upon return.

questions.question: What new transformation will God give to His people, as described in Ezekiel 11:19?
options: One heart and a new spirit, replacing their stony heart with a heart of flesh
Riches and power over nations
A new language and customs
A throne in the kingdom of heaven
questions.correctAnswer: One heart and a new spirit, replacing their stony heart with a heart of flesh
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:19 states that God will give them 'one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh,' symbolizing spiritual renewal.

questions.question: What is the intended outcome of the new heart and spirit given by God in Ezekiel 11:20?
options: That they may walk in God's statutes, keep His ordinances, and be His people
That they may conquer their enemies physically
That they may become wealthy and influential
That they may build a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: That they may walk in God's statutes, keep His ordinances, and be His people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:20 explains the purpose of the transformation: 'That they may walk in my statutes, and keep mine ordinances, and do them: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 11:21, how will God deal with those whose hearts follow detestable things and abominations?
options: He will recompense their way upon their own heads
He will forgive them without judgment
He will exile them to a distant land
He will make them leaders among the people
questions.correctAnswer: He will recompense their way upon their own heads
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:21 states, 'I will recompense their way upon their own heads,' indicating that God will bring consequences upon those who persist in evil.

questions.question: Where did the glory of the LORD stand after departing from the city, according to Ezekiel 11:23?
options: Upon the mountain which is on the east side of the city
On the temple roof
In the valley of the kings
At the western gate
questions.correctAnswer: Upon the mountain which is on the east side of the city
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:23 says, 'the glory of the LORD went up from the midst of the city, and stood upon the mountain which is on the east side of the city,' marking God's departure location.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 11:11 teach about the city and the people in relation to God's judgment?
options: The city shall not be their caldron nor the flesh in the midst thereof; judgment will occur at the border of Israel
The city will be their refuge and safe haven forever
They will be rewarded with peace in the city
The city will be destroyed without any survivors
questions.correctAnswer: The city shall not be their caldron nor the flesh in the midst thereof; judgment will occur at the border of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:11 clarifies that the city will not remain as their caldron nor flesh, but God will judge them at the border, showing a shift in the place of judgment.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 11:24, the spirit took Ezekiel in a vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea to the captives.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:24 states, 'the spirit took me up, and brought me in a vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea, to them of the captivity,' confirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 11:9 says God will deliver the people into the hands of strangers and execute judgments among them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:9 states, 'And I will bring you out of the midst thereof, and deliver you into the hands of strangers, and will execute judgments among you,' confirming this is true.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 11:25 reports that Ezekiel kept the vision to himself and did not speak to the captives about what the LORD showed him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:25 states, 'Then I spake unto them of the captivity all the things that the LORD had shewed me,' indicating Ezekiel did share the vision with the captives, making the statement false.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 11.

questions.question: What transformation does God promise to make in the hearts of the people in Ezekiel 11:19?
options: To give them a heart of stone
To give them one heart and a new spirit, replacing the stony heart with a heart of flesh
To multiply their hearts to increase understanding
To harden their hearts permanently
questions.correctAnswer: To give them one heart and a new spirit, replacing the stony heart with a heart of flesh
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:19 promises that God will give the people one heart and put a new spirit within them, taking away their stony heart and giving them a heart of flesh.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 11:20, what is the purpose of God giving the people a new heart and spirit?
options: So they may build houses and dwell securely
So they may walk in God's statutes, keep His ordinances, and be His people
So they may prosper in wealth and power
So they may conquer their enemies by force
questions.correctAnswer: So they may walk in God's statutes, keep His ordinances, and be His people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:20 states the purpose: that they may walk in God's statutes and keep His ordinances, becoming His people and He their God.

questions.question: What consequence does Ezekiel 11:21 declare for those whose hearts follow after detestable things and abominations?
options: They will be rewarded with riches
They will be recompensed upon their own heads
They will be forgiven and restored quickly
They will lead the people into battle
questions.correctAnswer: They will be recompensed upon their own heads
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:21 declares that those who follow detestable things will have their ways recompensed upon their own heads, meaning they will face judgment.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 11:22, what supernatural beings are described as lifting up their wings along with wheels beside them?
options: Seraphim
Cherubims
Angels of the Lord
Archangels
questions.correctAnswer: Cherubims
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:22 describes cherubims lifting their wings and the wheels beside them, a vision connected to God's glory.

questions.question: Where did the glory of the LORD stand after departing from the city as described in Ezekiel 11:23?
options: On the west side of the city
On the mountain on the east side of the city
Above the temple
In the valley outside the city
questions.correctAnswer: On the mountain on the east side of the city
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:23 states that the glory of the LORD went up from the city and stood upon the mountain on the east side.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'heart of flesh' replacing the 'stony heart' in Ezekiel 11:19 in relation to earlier scriptures such as Jeremiah 31:33?
options: It contradicts Jeremiah's prophecy of the new covenant
It echoes Jeremiah's promise of a new covenant with a transformed heart and spirit
It is unrelated to Jeremiah's writings
It fulfills the Mosaic Law perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes Jeremiah's promise of a new covenant with a transformed heart and spirit
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:19's promise of a heart of flesh parallels Jeremiah 31:33, where God promises a new covenant to put His law in their minds and write it on their hearts, indicating a unified theme of internal transformation.

questions.question: What vision did the Spirit bring Ezekiel to after the glory of the LORD departed, according to Ezekiel 11:24?
options: A vision of the new temple in Jerusalem
A vision in Chaldea to the captives
A vision of the end times
A vision of the destruction of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: A vision in Chaldea to the captives
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:24 explains that the Spirit took Ezekiel in a vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea (Babylon), to those in captivity.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 11:25, what did Ezekiel do with the vision he had seen?
options: He kept it secret
He spoke to the captives all the things the LORD had shown him
He destroyed the vision
He wrote a book about it
questions.correctAnswer: He spoke to the captives all the things the LORD had shown him
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:25 states that Ezekiel spoke to those in captivity all the things that the LORD had shown him in the vision.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage shares a similar promise of God putting a new spirit within people as found in Ezekiel 11:19?
options: Isaiah 53
Jeremiah 31:33
Genesis 12
Exodus 20
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 31:33
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:33 promises God will put His law within them and write it on their hearts, which parallels the new spirit and heart of flesh in Ezekiel 11:19.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Ezekiel 11:7 where the city is compared to a caldron and the people as the flesh inside it?
options: Simile
Metaphor
Alliteration
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:7 uses metaphor by describing the city as a caldron and the slain as flesh, symbolizing the city's judgment and destruction.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'heart of flesh' (lev basar) signify in Ezekiel 11:19?
options: A hardened, unyielding heart
A compassionate, responsive, and obedient heart
An unclean and sinful heart
A heart of stone
questions.correctAnswer: A compassionate, responsive, and obedient heart
questions.explanation: The Hebrew phrase 'lev basar' (heart of flesh) symbolizes a heart that is tender, responsive, and capable of obedience, contrasting with a 'stony' or hardened heart.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 11:15-16, how does God describe the scattered house of Israel in the countries among the heathen?
options: As forsaken and rejected forever
As a little sanctuary where God will be to them
As strangers to God
As completely destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: As a little sanctuary where God will be to them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:16 says that although God has cast them far and scattered them, He will be as a little sanctuary to them in the countries where they come.

questions.question: What is the significance of the east gate in Ezekiel 11:1 where the spirit lifted Ezekiel?
options: It symbolizes the place of God’s judgment and departure
It is the gate where the people enter to worship
It represents the entrance to the king’s palace
It is where the priests gather for sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the place of God’s judgment and departure
questions.explanation: The east gate, facing eastward, is significant as the place where Ezekiel saw the men conspiring and later where God's glory departed (Ezekiel 11:23), symbolizing judgment and divine departure.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 11:13, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died immediately after Ezekiel's prophecy against the leaders.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:13 states that Pelatiah died as Ezekiel was prophesying, showing the immediate judgment of God’s word.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 11:12 praises the people of Israel for following God's statutes and judgments faithfully.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:12 states the opposite: they did not walk in God's statutes nor execute His judgments, but followed the manners of the heathen.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which doctrine is primarily taught by the promise in Ezekiel 11:19-20 about giving the people one heart and a new spirit?
options: Regeneration and sanctification
Justification by faith alone
Predestination and election
Christ's atoning sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: Regeneration and sanctification
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:19-20 teaches God will remove the stony heart and give a heart of flesh, enabling obedience to His statutes; this signifies spiritual regeneration and sanctification. Cross-references: Ezekiel 36:26; Titus 3:5.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Ezekiel 11:16, where He promises to be a sanctuary to the scattered Israelites among the heathen?
options: God's mercy and faithfulness
God's wrath and judgment
God's omniscience
God's immutability
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy and faithfulness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 11:16 reveals God's mercy and faithfulness as He pledges to be a sanctuary for His scattered people despite their exile. Cross-reference: Psalm 46:1; Lamentations 3:22-23.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 11:7-8 teach about God's justice in relation to human sin and fear?
options: God executes judgment by bringing the sword upon the fearful sinners
God ignores human fear and punishes randomly
God rewards those who fear the sword
God removes all suffering from the city
questions.correctAnswer: God executes judgment by bringing the sword upon the fearful sinners
questions.explanation: These verses emphasize God's justice in bringing the sword upon those who feared it, showing that fear of judgment does not exempt one from punishment. Cross-reference: Romans 2:5; Hebrews 10:31.

questions.question: What combined theological insight is conveyed by Ezekiel 11:5-6 and 11:11 regarding the consequences of Israel's sin?
options: Sin leads to death and exile, severing them from their city as a place of blessing
Sin is inconsequential and leads to prosperity
God ignores sin because He is loving
Sin only affects the physical body, not the nation
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to death and exile, severing them from their city as a place of blessing
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 describe the many slain in the city due to sin, while verse 11 declares the city will no longer be their dwelling, teaching that sin results in death and exile. Cross-reference: Deuteronomy 28:63; Jeremiah 9:11.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 11:22-23, what is the significance of the glory of the LORD departing from the city and standing on the east mountain?
options: It symbolizes God's judgment and the loss of His presence among the people
It marks the beginning of a new temple construction
It indicates God's approval of the city
It shows God's immediate forgiveness and restoration
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes God's judgment and the loss of His presence among the people
questions.explanation: The departure of God's glory signifies His judgment and withdrawal of divine presence from Jerusalem, a pivotal moment in redemptive history. Cross-reference: 1 Kings 8:10-11; Revelation 21:23.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 11:13 teach about the relationship between prophecy and divine judgment?
options: The death of Pelatiah at the moment of prophecy shows divine confirmation of judgment
Prophecy is unrelated to actual events
Prophets have power to prevent judgment
Death is a sign of false prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: The death of Pelatiah at the moment of prophecy shows divine confirmation of judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 13 shows Pelatiah dying as Ezekiel prophesies, confirming God's judgment is imminent and certain. Cross-reference: Amos 3:7; Jeremiah 28:9.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s promises of restoration in captivity are merely wishful thinking. What does Ezekiel 11:24-25 actually teach about God's communication to the exiles?
options: God actively reveals visions and commands Ezekiel to speak to the captives, assuring restoration
God abandons the captives with no word of hope
Restoration is a human invention, not divine
The vision is vague and offers no assurance
questions.correctAnswer: God actively reveals visions and commands Ezekiel to speak to the captives, assuring restoration
questions.explanation: Verses 24-25 show God’s Spirit bringing Ezekiel to the captives to deliver His messages, affirming divine revelation and hope for restoration. Cross-reference: Jeremiah 29:10-11; Isaiah 40:1.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed in Ezekiel 11:17 where God promises to gather His scattered people and give them their land?
options: God's faithfulness and sovereignty
God's wrath and severity
God's ignorance
God's impatience
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness and sovereignty
questions.explanation: God’s promise to gather and restore Israel demonstrates His sovereign control over history and faithfulness to His covenant. Cross-reference: Isaiah 11:12; Jeremiah 31:10.

questions.question: What does the metaphor of the city as a caldron and the people as the flesh in Ezekiel 11:3 and 11:7 teach about the consequences of sin?
options: The city is a place of judgment where the people suffer as the contents of a boiling pot
The city is a place of refuge and safety
Sin purifies the people like metal in a furnace
The city is irrelevant to the people's fate
questions.correctAnswer: The city is a place of judgment where the people suffer as the contents of a boiling pot
questions.explanation: The caldron metaphor shows the city boiling over with judgment upon the sinful inhabitants, emphasizing impending destruction. Cross-reference: Jeremiah 1:13; Nahum 3:13.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching is illustrated by the distinction in Ezekiel 11:20-21 between those who walk in God's statutes and those who walk after their abominations?
options: The doctrine of divine recompense based on human obedience or disobedience
The doctrine of universal salvation
The doctrine of predestination without human responsibility
The doctrine of the inevitability of sin
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine recompense based on human obedience or disobedience
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 teach that God will bless those who obey and punish those who follow sinful ways, affirming just recompense. Cross-reference: Galatians 6:7; 2 Corinthians 5:10.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 11:9-10 contribute to the biblical narrative of exile and return?
options: It foretells Israel’s judgment by foreign nations but also recognition of God's sovereignty
It predicts permanent destruction with no hope
It denies any judgment on Israel
It encourages rebellion against foreign rulers
questions.correctAnswer: It foretells Israel’s judgment by foreign nations but also recognition of God's sovereignty
questions.explanation: The verses prophesy Israel's fall by sword and exile to strangers, culminating in acknowledgment of the LORD’s authority, fitting the exile-return motif. Cross-reference: 2 Kings 25:21; Daniel 9:2.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 11:15 reveal about the attitude of Jerusalem’s inhabitants toward the LORD and His people?
options: They reject the LORD and claim the land for themselves
They embrace the LORD wholeheartedly
They seek to make peace with the exiles
They are indifferent to divine commands
questions.correctAnswer: They reject the LORD and claim the land for themselves
questions.explanation: Verse 15 shows Jerusalem’s inhabitants telling the house of Israel to stay away from the LORD and asserting exclusive possession of the land, indicating rejection. Cross-reference: Jeremiah 7:4; Zechariah 7:11.

questions.question: What synthesis about divine omniscience and judgment is found by combining Ezekiel 11:5 and Ezekiel 11:21?
options: God knows all thoughts and will recompense individuals according to their ways
God is unaware of human plans and thus judgment is arbitrary
God forgives all without regard to deeds
God judges only external actions, not thoughts
questions.correctAnswer: God knows all thoughts and will recompense individuals according to their ways
questions.explanation: Verse 5 emphasizes God’s knowledge of all thoughts, while verse 21 promises recompense according to one’s ways, affirming omniscient and just judgment. Cross-reference: Hebrews 4:13; Romans 2:16.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 11:1 introduce the theme of leadership failure among Israel’s princes?
options: By naming princes who devise mischief and give wicked counsel
By praising the princes' faithfulness
By ignoring the princes completely
By describing their military victories
questions.correctAnswer: By naming princes who devise mischief and give wicked counsel
questions.explanation: Verse 1 introduces the princes Jaazaniah and Pelatiah as leaders involved in evil plotting, setting the stage for prophetic condemnation. Cross-reference: Ezekiel 8:10; Micah 3:1-3.

questions.question: What theological significance does Ezekiel 11:12 have regarding Israel's covenant disobedience?
options: Israel failed to walk in God's statutes and imitated surrounding heathen, breaking covenant
Israel perfectly kept the covenant
Israel's disobedience was due to ignorance
Israel's disobedience was irrelevant to God
questions.correctAnswer: Israel failed to walk in God's statutes and imitated surrounding heathen, breaking covenant
questions.explanation: This verse explicitly states Israel's failure to obey God's laws and the adoption of heathen customs, signifying covenant breach. Cross-reference: Deuteronomy 12:29-31; 2 Kings 17:7-12.
